reason: Ruff deliberately reports only `try` bodies that are a single simple statement, while flake8-simplify accepts any single statement; ~800 of the 850 flake8-only `try` bodies start with return (332), if (220), while (104), with (80), for (43).
evidence: PR #1948 "Restrict SIM105 to try blocks with a body of one simple statement" (fixes #1947: rewriting control flow with `contextlib.suppress` obfuscates the short-circuit); suppressible_exception.rs `matches!(try_body, [Stmt::Delete | Assign | AugAssign | AnnAssign | Assert | Import | ImportFrom | Expr | Pass])`.

reason: Ruff reports a chain of nested `with` statements once, at the outermost one (flake8-simplify reports every nested pair), and it also checks nested `async with`, which flake8-simplify ignores (most ruff-only reports).
evidence: ast_with.rs: "Make sure we fix from top to bottom for nested with statements... Parent will report SIM117 for this nesting"; repro: three nested `with` -> flake8-simplify 2 reports (2:5, 3:9), ruff 1; nested `async with` -> ruff only.

reason: Same finding, different anchor: pylint reports useless-return on the function definition, ruff on the trailing `return` statement; about 288 ruff-only/pylint-only pairs sit in the same function.

reason: pycodestyle's token heuristic only checks the name just before `=` or after for/as/global, so it misses ambiguous names inside tuple targets (`p, l, u = lu(a)`, `for s, l, b in ...`; ~400 ruff-only, the other 199 are lost-flake8-output artefacts), and it flags attributes (`self.l = lst`) and names used inside lambda bodies (the 74 flake8-only).
evidence: repro: `p, l, u = lu(a)` and `for s, l, b in xs` -> ruff E741, pycodestyle silent; `self.l = lst` and `raises(TypeError, lambda: RigidBody(P, (I, P)))` -> pycodestyle E741, ruff silent.

reason: Setup artefact: pep8-naming 0.15.1 has no N999 (module-name) check at all, so every ruff report is unmatched by construction; ruff files its own rule under the pep8-naming prefix.
evidence: pep8ext_naming.py contains no N999; `ruff rule N999`: "Derived from the **pep8-naming** linter"; pep8-naming#132 "Filename checks?" is still open.

reason: Ruff deliberately uses a heuristic (a direct base named `Exception` or ending in `Error`) instead of pep8-naming's walk through the module's class chain for `Exception`, so it flags subclasses of ValueError/FileNotFoundError/BotoCoreError (ruff-only) and misses subclasses of module-local exception classes such as werkzeug's HTTPException (flake8-only).
evidence: #783 (closed; charliermarsh: "let's do the latter for now (checking parent names) as a heuristic"); #20936 (open) asks for the recursive check; PR #24204 (closed, not merged).

reason: Ruff also reports the implicit-else form (`if c: return True` followed by `return False`, and the negated form), as its docs show; flake8-simplify only reports an `if` with an explicit `else`.
evidence: `ruff rule SIM103`: "Or, given: ... if x > 0: return True / return False ... Use instead: return x > 0"; flake8_simplify get_sim103 requires `get_returned_bool(node.orelse)`.

reason: Ruff only reports counters initialised to a literal 0 (documented) that are not used after the loop and not reassigned inside it (deliberate), while flake8-simplify reports any earlier assignment of the counter; secondary ANCHOR: flake8-simplify anchors on the initialisation and ruff on the `+= 1` (~97 pairs).
evidence: `ruff rule SIM113`: "In preview, this rule checks for index variables initialized with any integer rather than only a literal zero"; enumerate_for_loop.rs comments ("Ensure that the index variable was initialized to 0", "If there are multiple assignments to this variable within the loop, ignore it"); flake8_simplify get_sim113 reports `matches[0]` (the assignment).

reason: Ruff exempts @overload (302) and @override (4) signatures; the ruff-only are in pymupdf/src/__init__.py after its block-level `# pylint: disable=all` (89) and in functions under `# pylint: disable` pragmas (CFG).

reason: Ruff deliberately accepts a `...` body on the same line (`class C: ...`, `with x: ...`, `for x in y: ...`) for consistency with Black and ruff format: all 374 flake8-only lines end in `: ...`; 34 of the 42 ruff-only are lost-flake8-output artefacts and 8 are same-line `case` bodies, which pycodestyle does not recognise (REF).
evidence: PR #8499 "Allow collapsed-ellipsis bodies in other statements" (extends PR #2837 for classes, closes #8496); compound_statements.rs: "Allow `class C: ...`-style definitions".

reason: Harness artefact: all 276 ruff-only reports are in files whose flake8 output was lost (see N806); the 130 bugbear-only are bugbear false positives: it recognises infinite iterators only when spelled `itertools.cycle(...)` (not `it.cycle`, `from itertools import cycle, repeat`) and reports single-iterable `zip(x)` (REF).
evidence: bugbear.py `_is_infinite_iterator` requires `node.func.value.id == "itertools"`; repro `dict(zip(a, it.cycle(b)))`, `zip(a, cycle(b))`, `list(zip([25, 37]))` -> bugbear B905, ruff silent.

reason: Harness artefact: 340 of the 350 ruff-only reports are in files whose flake8 output was lost (see N806); the flake8-only are pyflakes false positives: strings inside subscripts read as forward references (`Annotated[int, "foo"]`, `Union["x", X]`, `TypedDict[({"key": int},)]`) and names defined through `global` in a function (numpy's vendored meson) (REF).

reason: Ruff deliberately does not count the function's own `def` (pylint starts every function at 1) but counts each nested `def` as a statement of the outer function, so counts near the threshold differ by one in either direction (88 pylint-only at 51/50).
evidence: PR #4794: "Pylint seems to include the `def` itself when counting the number of statements in a function, which feels off-by-one in practice. This PR removes that extra statement from the count."; repro `def f(): x = 1` -> ruff 1, pylint 2; babel tests/test_dates.py:1033 (two nested defs) -> ruff 51, pylint 50.

reason: Ruff only reports `len(x)` in a boolean test when x is syntactically known to be a sequence (a literal, or a name bound or annotated as list/dict/set/tuple/str/bytes, *args, **kwargs), while pylint reports `len(self)`, `len(obj.columns)` and other unresolved arguments.
evidence: `ruff rule PLC1802`: "Checks for `len` calls on sequences in a boolean test context"; len_test.rs: `// Simple inferred sequence type ...` `if !is_sequence(argument, semantic) && !is_indirect_sequence(argument, semantic) { return; }`.

reason: Ruff only checks `for` loops over names it can infer as dicts from literals or annotations, while pylint uses astroid inference and also checks comprehensions: ruff misses dicts that pylint infers (179) and comprehensions (63), and reports annotated dicts that pylint cannot infer (111); the comprehension gap is undocumented and untracked.
evidence: dict_index_missing_items.rs takes a `StmtFor` and returns `if !is_dict_literal && !is_inferred_dict(dict_name, checker.semantic())`; pylint recommendation_checker.py has `_check_consider_using_dict_items_comprehension`.

reason: Ruff only recognises `a < b and b < c` written with the shared operand adjacent, not reversed operands such as `x > 0 and x < y` or `c >= 0xFDD0 and c <= 0xFDEF`, which pylint normalises.
evidence: #29169 (open) "`boolean-chained-comparison` does not trigger when operands or condition order are reversed", PR #29189 (open); also #22206, #25041 (attributes); repro `if x > 0 and x < y` -> pylint R1716, ruff silent.

reason: Ruff checks many more file-opening calls than `open()` (io.open, tempfile.*, gzip.open, pathlib), as documented, and deliberately skips `open(...).close()`, opens inside a `with` item, `return open(...)`, ExitStack and enterContext calls, which flake8-simplify reports.
evidence: `ruff rule SIM115`: "The rule detects a wide array of IO calls where context managers could be used"; open_file_with_context_handler.rs comments: "Ex) `open(\"foo.txt\").close()`", "Ex) `return open(\"foo.txt\")`", "Ex) `with contextlib.ExitStack() as exit_stack`".

reason: Ruff's rule only compares a name (or a pure call on a name) with itself, while pylint compares any identical expressions: attribute chains (`transport.operations_client is transport.operations_client`, 208 in generated tests) and literals (which ruff covers under PLR0133).
evidence: `ruff rule PLR0124`: "Checks for operations that compare a name to itself."; comparison_with_itself.rs matches only `(Expr::Name, Expr::Name)` and single-name pure calls such as `id(foo)`.
